The name Omvati carries the meaning “Goddess of wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Omvati usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Omvati was an ancient Hindu goddess revered as the embodiment of fertility, love, and motherhood. She is often depicted with multiple arms, holding various symbols of prosperity and abundance, such as a lotus, a pot of rice, or a trident. One legend tells of how she was born from the tears of Shiva when he wept for the loss of his beloved wife, Sati.

Another story describes Omvati as a divine milkmaid who nourished the infant god Krishna with her abundant breast milk, symbolizing her role as a nurturing mother. She is also said to have married Krishna and bore him a son, Pradyumna.
